author: Billy
content:
All of the druids specs have a niche role.

I run 19/11/21 which is a twow take on what StormX, Final Flash/Cucker etc. have run in the past.  It's strength is killing potential at range, using feral charge for gap closer, interrupt, escapes in 1v2 etc. while still having NS heal. It's *very* gear dependent as well. https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid/P0X08I-UK06-ZW301 Vengeance/Natural Shapeshifter are flex points but Vengeance is nice if you can manage mana for shifting.

HOTW is based around similar flexibility as 19/11/21  https://talents.turtle-wow.org/druid/1-UK193EDO-ZW301 You will typically kill a bit slower as HOTW and be spending more time in bear/cat. Survivability can be higher in this build. You will be lacking Natural Weapons 3/3 for +hit. So you *will* need to get some hit on gear. HOTW is also a great choice if you like to do attrition fights to run people out of resources. It still has NS heal for self emergency or saving a teammate. I recommend keeping the 1 point in Nature's Grasp... 2/2 Feline Swfitness or 5/5 Heart of the Wild are flex points if you so choose instead.

Moonglow is basically a better healer with more mana conservation sources and more caster dps. However, the other two specs also conserve mana by sitting in bear to build mana back up so it's a trade. You will also lack Feral Charge which is imo one of the most useful druid abilities.

TLDR: 
19/11/21 -  for more caster dps with versatility.
HOTW - versatility + more survivability + more melee potential.
Moonglow - for focusing only on balance/resto, lacks Feral Charge for offensive/defensive options. 

Cheers.

author: Elesion
content:
I haven't done proper PvP in a long time but as a fairly old-school player I used to run a feral/resto hybrid build. My Blood Ring build was a homebrew 9/21/21. I too feel that hybrids are not nearly as strong as in Vanilla, but as gretchen mentioned mostly because pure feral is just so much stronger in a burst meta on TWoW (both due to mechanical/talent changes and because of lots of better gear).
It usually is a balancing act (as it probably should be). I've ended up 1 on 1 in BR a few times against other druids and my hybrid build (with mixed healing/tank gear) always won handily against deep feral because of better mana regen and more instant heals (time out of bear form is very dangerous). Rogues/warriors any druid should be able to eat for breakfast. But against casters deep feral does seem to have an edge. That's why I mixed in Berserk instead of Omen, for a little bit of burst at the opener and a second fear break.
And I totally don't agree that druids are bad pvp healers. We have the best mobility by far and the least chance of getting interrupted (counter spell, kick, pummel, earth shock) just because of our amazing arsenal of instant casts. Poly doesn't bother us, fear can be broken by trinket or Berserking, Blind can be abolish countered. Between keeping Reju on everyone, Swiftmend, Nature's Swiftness, 21s HoT from Regrowth... you can just run around like a madman keeping everyone topped off barely ever stopping to actually cast something. With Swiftmend and NS your ability to react to dangerous burst is unrivalled. If the enemy ignores you, they lose because you heal your team. If the enemy focusses you, they lose because you go bear or travel form. The ability to turn from the squishy healer into the tankiest target on the battlefield at the press of a button is huge. Druids might be the best PvP healers imo.

content:
It's not bad, Swift Travel Form is just almost useless.
__Advantages:__ You're immune to polymorph, you can use it to fake a heal spell and bait an interrupt, you can pre-cast it on a boat, it looks great, it comes from a sweet questline, you can use it to herb.
__Disadvantages:__ Same drawbacks as a mount (3s cast time, only outside, only out of combat) while not getting any mount speed bonuses (spurs, gloves enchant, trinkets) making it worse than plainsrunning, not even the PvP set bonus applies (which is specifically aimed at animal forms), it comes fairly late (palas and warlocks do their epic mount quest pre-raid while we need to full-clear ES - by that time in character progression most people probably have bought journeyman riding).
So yeah... do it for PvP or flavor, but for actual everyday travel you'll still be using a mount. My preferred fix would be make it instant cast like all other forms and disable it in battlegrounds (like plainsrunning), keep the out-of-combat requirement. Then it would be awesome for short distances and I would use it all the time.

author: Dexter Syphex
content:
Multiple Target Priority (AoE):

Strong tanks: Open with Moonfire on all targets.
Weaker tanks: Open with Insect Swarm, then apply Moonfire.
Mobs die <12 seconds: Use Moonfire only.
Mobs live >16 seconds: Apply both Moonfire and Insect Swarm to maximize damage.
5+ targets: After spreading DoTs (following above rules), channel Hurricane 3 seconds into the pull for maximum AoE damage while tanks secure threat.

Follow raid target priorities, but when your current target reaches 35% HP, either:
Focus it with Wrath until it dies OR
Switch to the next assigned target and adjust your rotation.

Openers:
Precast Wrath 1.3 seconds before the pull to avoid early aggro and help trigger Arcane Eclipse quickly. Avoid Starfire as it can instantly pull threat.
Cast 2 Wraths, then follow the single-target priority rotation.
Use DPS trinkets during Arcane Eclipse unless an immediate burst is needed to avoid a wipe.

content:
I think the most important factors don't have anything to do with stats.

These are the things I noticed other boomies doing wrong that put me ahead in the same raid.

1. Uptime
Always try to be doing sth. look for which mobs the tank might pull next and try to be in range once he does. This seems trivial but 90% of players don't havw good uptime.

2. Movement.
Move in a way that lets you hardcast as much as possible and move as little as possible. If you have to use an instant think where you might rather be and move a bit towards that point during gcd.

3. Dots
Dots are underutilized. They just have better dmg per cast than our hardcasts, especially on lower crit/gear levels. Some people here will disagree but if they did the math they wouldnt. Make sure to consider if a mob will live long enough for the dot to do its thing though.
These are also really good for optimizing uptime. You can pretty much always apply IS on any mob the tank pull immediatly. If you're not worried about aggro use mf.

4. Consumes
Consumes add more than one tier level of gear difference in player power. Except for flask my consume expenses are usually covered by raid gold so I make sure to use as much as possible.

5. Managing Hurricane CD
We only really have Hurricane as a AOE cd. You should try to calcualte how many mobs it takes for hurricane to be worth using and then use it as much as possible. Make sure its up for especially big pulls.

6. Gear
At this point gear matters and you should look at it. There are some tools for this pinned in this channel. But if you understand you want crit, hit and spellpower you are already pretty good on this. People always overestimate how much optimizing between these 3 stats matters. If you can swap gear to go from 13% hit,20% crit to 10% hit, 23% crit it will never fix why boomie feels weak for you.

These things may sound obvious but I 100% think they make all the difference between a player being dragged along and one carrying. If you do these well you will notice the difference because almost nobody does.

author: Lyrazia
content:
So. The way energy works (cat resource to cast spells) is that we get it in 'ticks' every 2 sec we get 20 energy.
But what you can do is that you got en enchant (it was a helm in classic) & a talent (furor) which made it so entering cat form yields 60 energy. 
Doing so only needs 1 GCD (Global cooldown, GCD is what determines how quick every class can use spells, when using a GCD spell, all spells have a period where they can't be used)
So the most effective way of gaining energy and thus being able to use more spells is that you hit 0 energy and then before you get the 20 energy from a tick, you leave cat form and reenter it. Thus you end up getting 80 energy, (60 from entering cat form and 20 from the tick) and then you can use your main damage spell more during a fight

author: Julchat
content:
Hi, I bring a solution for tree druids that want to use healbot addon. 
I tried searching for one on this discord but couldn't find a solution for it so...

Problem: Whilst in combat in Tree of Life form, HealBot "disables" your healing bars. This happens because back then in Vanilla Tree of Life wasn't a thing, so it was safe to say that if you were shapeshifted then you couldn't cast healing spells. This is not the case in Turtle WoW due to added content, bringing Tree of Life to a Vanilla WoW version.

Solution: Change your HealBot.lua file in the HealBot Addon folder. Search for the function called **HealBot_GetShapeshiftForm()**, erase it, and use this function implementation instead

> function HealBot_GetShapeshiftForm()
>   local forms = GetNumShapeshiftForms();
>   if forms then
>     for i = 1, forms do
>       local icon, name, active = GetShapeshiftFormInfo(i);
>       if active then
>         local iconLower = string.lower(icon or "")
>         local nameLower = string.lower(name or "")
>         if not string.find(iconLower, "humanoidform") and
>            not string.find(iconLower, "tree") and
>            not string.find(nameLower, "tree") then
>           return i;
>         end
>       end
>     end
>   end
>   return nil;
> end

What this does basically is ignoring Tree of Life as a shapeshift form, as the addon already did with "Humanoid Form"
Then, for the addon, you will probably be considered as being in Humanoid Form.

Dunno if that change brings more errors/bugs to the addon, but from my short personal testing, it hasn't.
And yes, with that, you can now use HealBot in Tree of Life form (not healing touch ofc).

Keywords for search: Tree form HealBot Tree of Life Tree Shapeshift

author: Micro Jackson
content:
Giving general advice is kind of hard without context. You can look into my stats here: https://www.turtlogs.com/armory/character/Turtle%20WoW%20Nordanaar/Allerrias
You will see that as a druid you shouldn't really be at the bottom, you should be at the top of healing.

As general advice, you can start healing before the fight starts.
I always put HOTS on the tanks before they pull.
This is the biggest part of druid healer, once you have enough experience, you know in what fight when and who gets damaged, and you can prehot them all, and on some fights I can't predict, so I put rank 7 rejuvs on everyone instead. I can spam rank 7 for eternity without losing mana.
Regrowth is amazing with it's HOT, and has the most powerful swiftmend you can get.
Putting a HOT on people when there is no raid damage is pointless, the flash spammers will heal them faster then your heals can tick, just focus on something else, or use a low rank regrowth to tick some people off, but it's 2.0 seconds cast time instead of the flash spammers 1.5s, so your probably always too late.

P.S. It's also heavily based on how good your other healers are.
If they are really good healers, you will heal less.

author: Medvedev
content: AQ40 will put your focus a lot more towards physical mitigation. The magic damage bursts from the dragon breaths in BWL is replaced with harder hitting physical damage. Many encounters will encourage you to focus on mitigation much more than threat output. Make sure you've prepared high armor budget options for all your secondary gear slots, that is cloak, 2x rings, 2x trinkets, and a neck if you really want to safe it. It may be needed for multiple encounters, especially during progression.

author: 𝓜𝓲𝓭𝓸𝓴𝓸 ฅ₍^◕ᴥ◕^₎ฅ
content: its a very different game here on turtle with other classes being boosted to TBC levels practically, the old school "war of attrition" style of fighting as druid is much, much harder. Still viable in open world/bg 1v1s where you can actually outrange arcane mages and kite paladins endlessly, but not in duels where you have limited space. Balance Druid got its turtle power boost in the form of standing still and turreting spells which doesnt translate as well to pvp as other classes additional power. Simply put your hots and dots can't outlast the insane damage people can do very quickly here they way you can on vanilla. You can have some success with that build in BGs, but imo you're better off dropping the feral tree for moonkin form, more damage, and more range. Also i would take mana efficiency over Gift of Nature because the additional healing is only applied to base healing values and isn't affected by gear, and dampening in bg's makes it even worse.

author: Micro Jackson
content:
Not even close for druids or priests stacking spirit.
A bunch of gear has +meditation% like the meditation ring from Loatheb.
For priests it's MP2 = (spirit / 4) + 13.
For druids it's MP2 = (spirit / 5) + 15.
MP5 = MP2 * 2.5
And then 10% of that for what that ring gives you.
So with 500 spirit which is easy to get raid buffed:
(500 / 4) + 13 * 2.5 / 10 = 34,5 MP5 or 28.5 MP5 for druids.

But it's a nice ring for when you get it.

to me the tanks kind of historically fill the themes of:

- Bear: highest single target threat, not good aoe, high HP, huge damage intake, bad defensive options. Can easily flex to Cat, pragmatically easy to gear.
- Prot paladin: good mit, insane aoe, good defensive options, lower hp.
- Shammy: spell tank? good aoe tank too, good threat, not amazingly tanky though.

author: Hotverdomme-Nord
content:
I wasn't here when it was written, but it was kinda discussed yesterday. You basically fall into 4 topics.
1. Go back to the old SF buff, which I don't think they want.
2. A complete rework of BoaT that doesn't require the dots, frontloads the dots, or limit the impact of BoaT/dots and buff other things, for the next balancing patch in 6 months or whatever (If the server stays).
3. The cast time of SF in PVE, with ebb and 3.5 is okay on bosses, but could use a small adjustment to make it feel better, but without the 0.2 and extra crit for NG it doesn't feel nearly as good as it does for bis gear. You do have the clunkyness of not having moonfire up for a SF during eclipse or for the spell afterwards, if you don't proc eclipse early or you mismanaged your moonfire.
4. In PVP the old BoAT was awesome even with it's one flaw! Against specific targets it's close to impossible to use SF on shaman, melee, and hunters, barkskin is needed and it means Starfire in worst case scenarios end up at 3.8 and GL living that long and not have it interrupted, grounded, FD:d, pet stun or scatter. In otherwords when they are on you forget about it, you can't cast that spell, especially in arena or vs multiple players, where players aren't completely braindead and try to face tank everything. We also have no dispel protection so against someone that can dispel one of our most important talents become useless.
TL:DR; in PVE the change on trash is whatever, on ST bosses it's mostly a feel thing unless you need a lot of movement and/or fast dmg. On multiple targets that you can use it on it's a massive dps loss and machine gun SF are fun. In PVP SF is incredibly garbage, especially since roots break without dmg and everyone have tools or structures to avoid it completely with little to no difficulty, because nobody stays to wait for a 2.8 sec cast, 3.8 with barkskin  (barkskin is awful).
